steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...The rising of the Urticas' secret chamber destroyed the original plate of Ludwigs-Universität. Coupled with the influence of Herkunftshorn's Arts, the school can no longer function normally.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: For now, the Empresses' Voice have taken over the cleanup operation from the Gendarmerie. Unaffected students and faculty have been relocated to neighboring Ostendorfhof.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The cleanup will take about a week. Thereafter, they will be able to return to campus...

No need. Ludwigs-Universität's library will be relocated to Neuleopoldshof and fall under the purview of the Reichsmuseum. The other campuses and faculties will be merged into the Reichskunstakademie in Bachshof.
The Gesatzswächter will be in charge of disposing of all of the remaining plates belonging to Urtica.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But then Ludwigs-Universität will—

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Ludwigs-Universität will become history.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Your Majesty...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Are you surprised?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: When I received the summon, I thought—

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: You thought I would be Lieselotte.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My apologies.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: You did well. Lieselotte thinks very highly of you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Danke schön, Your Majesty. If you hadn't graced us with your presence yesterday...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: It's behind us, no need to speak of it again.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Your Majesty... there is one other thing.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Arturia... the wanted Sankta, I bumped into her, and she mentioned my father.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I would like to know if she had something to do with his death. If you would permit me...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: We've been over this, Hochberg.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: The case of the Witch King's remains stealing a copy of the Güldenesgesatz has been closed.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Brandt.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Your Majesty, you are here as well.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Have you come to see Cora?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: She is currently rehearsing the Güldenesgesatz. The delay caused by the Witch King's remains has us all worried about tomorrow's performance.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Rest assured, the Movement is flawless at all times.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Cora said the same. How long have you gone without a break? Why not take a vacation after the Celebration?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You could go back to Sturmland together. Not as a Reichsorchester tuner and Gesatzswächter, but as Cora and Brandt.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: This is a reward, not a punishment. For mopping up the Witch King's remains. You and Viviana have done fine work, and I've taken notice.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Just remember that... opportunity does not last forever. Some things must be said before it's too late.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Thank you, Your Majesty, for the reminder.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: And another thing, I'll need at least twenty Gesatzswächter for tomorrow's Celebration.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Does Grimmacht know about this...?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Every year, Das Kaiserinnensfest begins with Reichsorchester's performance of the Güldenesgesatz, and ends with my duet with Hildegard.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: I wonder.... This year, will the people still appreciate our performance?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...I have no doubt, Your Majesty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Could I ask you a question, Brandt?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Assume your most prized possession has a crack in it. Would you... turn a blind eye to it? Pretend you didn't notice?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You're going to leave Zwillingstürme?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia is under control. I will return to Laterano and report to His Holiness the Pope. We will subsequently seek formal legal cooperation from Leithanien.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Alright. But I should remind you... tomorrow is Das Kaiserinnensfest.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Zwillingstürme will be very lively. Young people from other regions, even other countries, will all join in the merrymaking.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Correct, I had noticed an increase in foot traffic.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: And so, I want to ask... Herr Executor, won't you stay just one more day?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please explain why I'd do that.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Um... Arturia has been apprehended, the copy of the Güldenesgesatz has been recovered, and the Witch King's remains have been more or less wiped out. It seems like everything's all taken care of, but I can't shake this uneasy feeling.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Grimmacht says I have a unique sense for danger... I mean, of course, it might just be my imagination.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: For matters pertaining to internal Leithanian affairs, I suggest you confer with your empress.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: She's been too busy to see me today.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: So that's why you have time to escort me out of the city? I had assumed this was an official duty.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: A duty? No, it's not my duty to monitor you.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: And, err, having come all the way to Zwillingstürme, wouldn't you like to stay a bit longer? Make some new friends? See the sights?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Friends and sights...

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Are you looking at... that coffee shop?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I could try the drink Loris recommended before I leave.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: H-Herr Sankta!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are Yulia's brother, Jan. Do you work at this coffee shop?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Ja, I need to save money so I can study abroad when I'm ready. I thought I'd never see you again.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: I've heard that the executors of the Lateran Notarial Hall carry out the wills of Lateran citizens, is that right?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: An acceptable summary.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: And you also... solve cases?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: So long as it is part of a binding document, I will do everything in my power to carry it out.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Wunderbar! Loris left me a key before he died. He said there were clues about my sister's case in his house.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: But I'm not a detective after all, and wasn't sure who to give the key to.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is the residence of Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: This is a home in Zwillingstürme! You've barely known Bordin for an afternoon and he left you his entire house?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What he left me are clues to a case.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Look—The wall, the table, the drawers, everywhere.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: These are all clues regarding Yulia Schüler, the girl who disappeared over ten years ago.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And... a letter.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris claimed to have accepted defeat. But actually, he never gave up on the case.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I almost forgot that you're a case-solving machine. Even if they made you a Graf and granted you the tallest spire in Zwillingstürmeshof, you'd hardly blink, would you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A false premise, that is. There is no precedent for a Lateran saint being conferred a title by another country.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: And what do you have to do with Lateran sainthood...? Are you suggesting that you, Herr Executor, bear the title of Saint?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Like the Founders and the Popes?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am unclear on what you mean by 'like' in this context, but nominally yes.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: ...I may need to reevaluate our need to monitor you, Herr Saint.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are an 'executor' to an empress. I had assumed you had some familiarity with my background.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I thought I did too.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do not worry. Whether or not I hold the title of saint is not particularly relevant to my work in Leithanien.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My executorial duty is to capture Arturia, as well as executing the wills of Lateran citizens.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As the Arturia case is on temporary hold, fulfilling the will of Loris Bordin is my next objective.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Was that... hesitation? I've never seen you hesitate before!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I still have questions about the Arturia case.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What questions?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I need to think.
Federico looks at the piano to the side of the room.
Like most Leithanians, Loris had musical instruments in his home. However, judging from the many files and folders on its bench, he did not play the piano often.

Simply tap the black and white keys in a certain rhythm and a melody will be created. People have taken such immediate feedback for granted, yet there are still many questions that, once sprouted, are pushed away, unanswered.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: The piece you just played... is it the one from yesterday at Ludwigs-Universität?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Der Tod des Hexenkönigs.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia interpreted the emotions of Loris Bordin and Brandt Reiner, as well as the others who witnessed the Witch King's demise. She turned their strongest feelings into notes, creating this piece.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I want to know what she discovered in those emotions.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: The notes may be the same, but the feelings are so different.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Herr Executor, are you and Arturia really related by blood? If misplaying an instrument were a crime, you might well be arrested as soon as you step out the door.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I did not play a single note wrong.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: But there was no emotion whatsoever! You can't grasp music by memorizing its rules. You have to... um... picture the emotion it conveys.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: For example, Loris Bordin. You have to become him, imagine the night he charged into the Witch King's Spire. Picture how he became a hero, how crestfallen he was by Yulia's case, and...

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: When you're finally forced to doubt yourself, and find yourself wavering, lost, like me... you'll realize that you need a strength, a reason.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And that's when you'll discover that the law offers no guidance.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Why do barriers never cease to be? Is mankind doomed never to understand one another?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The tiniest chaos is enough to shatter the order. The moment confusion envelops, people begin to hurt one another...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Each era has its own trials and tribulations, for which we can only prepare to the best of our ability. It is certain, however, that you have been chosen because It believes that you have the ability to respond to the unknown.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You are well aware that there is another besides yourself very unique among the Sankta.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Bring her back, if possible. I need to meet with her, face to face.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, your whole life, you have been different, different from all the others.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Can you really... not see everything I see in the music?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Thanks to Grimmacht, both my ears and my soul have been saved.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: A failed attempt, I take it? Let's not try that again. We have to acknowledge that some people simply lack the talent for music.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes, I cannot empathize with Loris or anyone else, nor do I see the illusions created by the notes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But I do have realized that emotions are also information.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What do you mean by that?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As you said, Arturia's performances are completely different from mine. The notes arranged in order have no inherent meaning, but with added emotion, they become a piece of music beloved by you people.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: And so, I have come to understand that emotion is a kind of additional information.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia played her music, playing the hearts of Loris and others, to extract information from their powerful emotions that even they themselves could not retrieve.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is something only Arturia can do.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Her objective has not yet been achieved, nor will she abandon it. There will be even greater chaos in the coming days, here in Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: ...Are you certain?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I could spend time explaining the finer logic to you, but I assess that you will find it difficult to share my thought process. As such, I suggest you consider my conclusion a kind of... intuition.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Herr Executor, there is someone you should see. She can help you.
Congratulations, you're about to be rid of me.

What, I shouldn't say such things? What would you rather hear? Mockery, anger, curses? Or a seemingly invincible enemy pulled straight from a story begging for mercy before their departure from the stage?
Don't forget, you wanted to see me. Whenever you have doubts, you unconsciously seek out my voice.

spans.text: wanted to see me. Whenever you have doubts, you unconsciously seek out my voice.

steps.text: You want to hear me deny you, and then, in denying me, you can win some silly comfort for yourself.

spans.text: You want to hear me deny you, and then, in denying
, you can win some silly comfort for yourself.

steps.text: It is not I who needs you. You need me.
Bloodline of Urtica, Franz, Ebenholz——Without me, what does your future hold?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: It's done.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What do you mean...? What's done?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: I've removed the Voice of Mundane from your head.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: But nothing happened, is that it? It could never summon the Genesis Horn in the first place!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: It's like watching a crowd of people nervously gathering to light a fuse and blow Zwillingstürme up, only to hear a soft pop like a gloompincer's depressing fart.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But didn't you say the melody of the Witch King could open the door to the Genesis Horn?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Yes, the right melody. Do you think you can open a locked door with any old key?! Don't compare my research on Herkunftshorn with the pile of rubbish they stuffed into your brain.

spans.text: melody. Do you think you can open a locked door with any old key?! Don't compare my research on Herkunftshorn with the pile of rubbish they stuffed into your brain.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Those idiots and their Infected bombing couldn't manage a thing!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Ha, 'The Voice of Mundane'... Do the people who come up with this stuff even know the difference between a proper creation and a belch?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Was it Gerhard who filled your heads with all this? Would you mind if I dug him up and knocked him around a bit more?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But they told me the Voice of Mundane housed the Witch King's avatar.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Avatar? Haha... avatar.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: That'd be like me rolling my soul into a ball and tossing it into the amphitheater beneath the spire for you stupid lambs to kick about. You really think that can be done?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: That's enough, boy. I'm in a bad mood, a positively rotten one. I thought by doing this one last favor for Grimmacht, I'd be able to take my things and finally be rid of this wretched place.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Who'd have thought those masked morons would make a fool of me... No, they made me a whole circus!

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: I should have Ermengarde look me over, see if a Lich's age has any effect on his brain.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He said... The Voice of Mundane is just noise.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It is certainly a melody left by the Witch King, that's true. But Gerhard and his men misunderstood its power. It isn't the key to the Witch King's legacy.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then what about the... voice in my head?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I don't understand the Arts behind it.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The problem of the Voice of Mundane has been resolved. You may still suffer headaches and hallucinations, but I expect they won't be so bad going forward.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Just to be safe, you should stay here and rest a while. Then leave Zwillingstürme after Das Kaiserinnensfest.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So, the voice is just my imagination then?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: All these years, and all of my struggles were just in my head? In the somewhat more figurative sense?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Apparently, I have nothing whatsoever to do with any grand plans of those lofty conspirators.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And to speak of killing myself before I went mad... Hah, I've been mad for a long, long time.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I don't have time to discuss this with you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Right.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You grandfather says that the rubbish in my head tainted the research on Herkunftshorn. So why care about me, an inferior product? Particularly after we've known that none of his power lies within me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I can't summon a Catastrophe cloud with a wave of my hand, nor can I cleave a spire with a swing of a sword—

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What do you want?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The power is still there. Since you've removed the Voice of Mundane, why not... kill me?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Voice of Mundane is not the key, meaning I'm of no use to the Twin Empresses. Why not burn me and mine to ashes, like all the experiments of the Witch King era?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Because there is no...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...No need? Is that it?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then what about my brother? He died. He died because of a stupid plan like... To borrow a phrase, like a gloompincer's depressing fart. Such nonsense... such irony!

spans.text: Then what about my brother? He died. He died because of a stupid plan like... To borrow a phrase, like a gloompincer's depressing fart. Such nonsense... such

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He was grateful, you know, right up until he died... Grateful for our meeting, grateful for the instructor who taught him the cello.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But our meeting was exploited by Gertrude. The teacher he admired was mixed up with the Witch King's remains.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hah, and now you tell me... you tell me the Voice of Mundane was all a wacky misunderstanding the entire time!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So we lived, died, met, parted, all for what? Where is the meaning in any of it?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Alright, if you want an answer, I'll tell you.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You're right. There was no meaning in any of it.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Set aside the Urtica name. Without the Voice of Mundane, you're nothing but a self-absorbed, self-harming, self-destructive empty shell of a pretty boy.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Perfect. You finally did it.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Now take up your Arts Unit.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why not unwrap the bandages on your sword? That would make this execution go even smoother.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The man before me is unworthy of it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Even now, you just have to humili—

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Then fight back. Prove me wrong by your actions.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You loathe the bloodline of the Witch King. But have you ever sought out the victims of his persecution? To make amends, to help them, to compensate them?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You loathe the title of Graf Urtica. But have you ever looked into the safety of the commoners? Taken note of the decline of your domain, caught between the Twin Empresses and the Witch King's remains?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You lament being the only survivor. But you have not been cherishing the life ahead of you. Instead, you constantly throw yourself into danger.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You say you were a prisoner of your spire. But who, in the end, has never looked beyond his cage at anyone else?
Lessing's sword moves so quickly that dodging is nearly impossible. He's rarely spoken so many words in one breath.
At first, Ebenholz had no intention of dodging, but almost instinctively, the Originium dice float into the air. Arts pour out uncontrollably, like fiery rage.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Blood, title, duty, everything was forced upon me by fate.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I tried! I stood against it! And in the end, you tell me there was never any need to!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why? Why did I have to go through all this when I'm nobody at all?
Lessing's sword presses against Ebenholz's throat. The Originium dice fall to the side.
The battle is over, the outcome a surprise to no one.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Our fight against fate never belonged to any of us. And so, what does the suffering we've endured... even count for?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I never received a noble's education, and I don't throw around words like 'fate.'

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I only know that all the suffering is real.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I've seen street hawkers beaten by the Gendarmerie in the alleyways. I've seen old men freeze to death on the roadside after losing their farmland to the rural nobility.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: They'll never see the Witch King, the Twin Empresses, or a Kurfürsten in their life. They'll never have the time or energy to contemplate fate, suffering, or meaning.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: That's life in the shadow of the spires, for the great masses of Leithanien.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: No one can overcome an abstract concept. If you want revenge, choose a concrete target. The Witch King, the Twin Empresses, the still living remnants.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: We fight to survive. And we don't stop until our own blood or that of our enemies runs dry.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Fight...

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The Witch King's legacy still exists, wherever it is. Enemies shrouded in darkness may find it at any moment, and use it to unleash suffering on the great masses once again.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: You can stay in this spire and continue lamenting your 'fate,' or you can challenge me again and die by my hand.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Or... you can join me in seeking the Witch King's legacy. Help me find the true culprit, who may still be alive in some form.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Choose.
Ebenholz feels the sword against his throat, still wrapped in bandages. Were it not wrapped, he would have smelled blood.
Of course, this does not mean that Lessing can't kill him. The warrior's expression is cold, but his eyes burn with anger.
Why is he angry?
Why... does he still have expectations for a man like him?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Would you kindly pass me my Arts Unit?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why aren't they here?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Frau Hochberg, what is it you're looking for?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Sketches... Frieda Seemann's drawings.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Since Herr Reiner and I left, has anyone else been in this room?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Um... no suspicious individuals, meine Dame.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: After you and Herr Gesatzswächter left, the Imperial casters carefully inspected the entire alley.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: After confirming no traces of the Witch King's remains, and no dangerous witchcraft or items, they left.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Are the drawings you're looking for involved in some important case?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A case?
Viviana recalls Grimmacht's words.
'The case of the Witch King's remains stealing a copy of the Güldenesgesatz has been closed.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's merely personal. Frau Seemann's work is incredibly beautiful. It always evokes some... marigold memories in me.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Please don't alert the others though. I don't want too many people to know I've been here.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Of course! Rest assured. The Gendarmerie will never disclose your movements.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: So lovely. Marigolds, sunlight... such beautiful things tend to inspire creativity and nurture emotion.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: No wonder so many Leithanian artists love this alley. Werner von Hochberg... He was obsessed with it until the day he died.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Might you be... Frau Giallo? Weren't you taken away by Grimmacht's casters?

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: I'm certainly not here.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: And you didn't really bump into your father back there either.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: This is all in your imagination.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Is this also an effect of your Arts?

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: You're rather skilled in Originium Arts yourself. What do you think?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I... haven't noticed anything unusual.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: People often misunderstand my Arts. The truth is, I can't do very much at all. People are just ignorant of their own hearts. Or even if they do know, they're unwilling to face themselves.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: I told you the first time we met. My melodies resonate with the emotions deep inside the human heart... and once they ripple, they are hard to ignore.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: It's you who wants to change your father's fate. The one talking to you now, well, I'm afraid it's you yourself.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Is that so?

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: You yearn to know the cause of your father's death.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: You fear that the conspiracy of the Witch King's remains is not yet through. You suspect that the farce performed at Ludwigs-Universität was just a diversion.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: You wonder... if perhaps the Kaiserinnen wanted to kill the Kurfürst?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Nein.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: Ah, but you see, you can't hold back the birth of this thought.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: If your father were standing here, what would he do?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My father...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He wouldn't do anything.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He would accept fate's plan, and turn away.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: Even though he would go on to live with endless pain and regret.

steps.name: 'Arturia'
steps.text: And so, what about you? Would you... do the same?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: He and I...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Giallo?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do not mistaken me for that distant relative of mine. There is no need for you to brandish your Arts Unit in my direction.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...This whole area is encircled by Leithanien's finest Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Who are you, Herr Sankta?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am an executo— I work with Michael.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Michael is a good boy. I guess... I can trust you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That went surprisingly well.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: At Michael's suggestion, I would like to provide a clue regarding Arturia.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There is a high probability that she is planning an even more serious incident.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Seniora Viviana von Hochberg, it is my hope that we can cooperate, and put a stop to her plans.
